elements.title: flag of Okinawa Prefecture (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the white ring on the flag of Okinawa Prefecture (pictured) represents the "O" in "Okinawa"?

elements.title: Mahra Al Maktoum (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Emirati princess Mahra Al Maktoum invoked the triple talaq to divorce her husband, which is traditionally done only by the husband?

elements.title: prisoners of war in World War II (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that as many as 35 million soldiers became prisoners of war in World War II, according to some estimates?

elements.title: Luigi Mangione (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Luigi Mangione was described as "somewhat of an online sex symbol" following his December 2024 arrest?

elements.title: Mseilha Fort (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Mseilha Fort is strategically located to overlook the crossing of the Jaouz River near Ras ash-Shaq'a, a promontory in Lebanon?

elements.title: Saint Amata of Assisi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Saint Amata of Assisi was interviewed and testified during the process of the canonization of her aunt, Saint Clare of Assisi?

elements.title: the school's TV station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that journalism students at New Mexico State University were willing to work for free to save their newscast on the school's TV station?

elements.title: Rockwell PPS-8 (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Rockwell PPS-8 microprocessor had a number of features that made Adam Osborne call it "most unusual" and "difficult to understand"?

elements.title: a president of the Oregon Senate (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a president of the Oregon Senate crawled along a ledge of the State Capitol to access an unsecured window of the absent governor's office to place bills on his desk?
